measurement: v1.35 hand inspection of the v1.26 uninspected residue (docs/measurements/v126-uninspected-residue.json)
population: all 112 ids in the residue; none skipped
method: Per entry: Sudachi (SplitMode.C, .venv-jp) on exJP against exKana; exTokens concatenation against exJP and exKana; the audio arbiter (check_forces_reading.py / check_dictation_readings.py, caches outside the repo) where a reading was in doubt; the inspector's own judgement of naturalness, sense and both translations. Every defect was then put to two independent refuters; a correction ships only when both upheld it. Each row carries the inspector's evidence in full and its confidence, regenerated from the raw inspection results; rows the refuters decided also carry 'disposition', 'refuterVotes' and 'resolution' (what was decided and changed).
note: 'ok' means no defect was found by this method, not that the sentence is proven; 'uncertain' rows are recorded and unchanged. v126-uninspected-residue.json is left as it is: this is a one-time hand inspection, and those 112 sentences are still outside every automated reading gate.

items.current: できる / できる; 私は日本語で話すことができます。 / わたくしはにほんごではなすことができます
items.proposed: None under the house rule. If the owner ever revisits the 私 register class: exKana わたしはにほんごではなすことができます and exTokens [私, わたし]. That is one token, and the manifest must record it because exKana and exTokens are write-once.
items.evidence: The headword span でき(る) is read correctly, and ことができる matches the 'to be able to' sense. The one reading question is the non-headword 私, read わたくし. Sudachi reads ワタクシ, which is where the exKana came from. The audio arbiter, run from scratch copies with scratch caches, put わたし nearest at DTW 0.05369 against わたくし at 0.06645. Byte-identical proof was silent. The same run reproduced the n2-b304 control (みっか 0.00580 vs さんにち 0.06541). The repo already records this sentence in dictation-reading-mismatches.json as '私 わたくし -> わたし', proven (v1.29, instrument 1b), and it is excluded from dictation (v129-nearest-exclusions.json). In my own judgement わたし is the expected N5 reading in this neutral です/ます sentence, but わたくし is real Japanese. PLAN-V1.25 explicitly declines rewriting 私/わたくし where 私 is not the headword ('Register, not error'), and 私 ships both readings at N5 (n5-g012 わたし, n5-b378 わたくし). So under the house standard this is not a defect. It is reported here so it is visible.

items.current: 来る / くる; 友達が来ます。 / ともだちがきます; exEN 'My friend comes.' / exZH 朋友来了。
items.proposed: Translations only, no change to exJP/exKana/exTokens: exZH 朋友要来。 (or 朋友会来。). Optionally exEN 'My friend is coming.' (or 'My friend will come.').
items.evidence: The reading is correct. Sudachi gives 来:き, the irregular ます-stem, matching exKana. The arbiter reads it the taught way: き 0.04085 vs く 0.07332 vs こ 0.08789, where the rivals are nonsense forms used as a negative control. PLAN-V1.26 already names this as a correct irregular. Tokens round-trip. The only issue is tense in the translation. 来ます is non-past (will come / is coming), while 朋友来了 is read first as perfective or change-of-state, 'my friend has come / is here'. That could teach a Chinese-speaking learner that 来ます means 'came'. 了 can also announce an arrival in progress, so this is my own judgement of a minor mismatch, not a clear error. The English 'My friend comes.' is correct in tense but stilted.
items.resolution: Reading correct (来:き). exZH 朋友来了 may read as perfective against non-past 来ます; 了 can also announce an arrival, so a low-confidence tense note only. No change.

items.current: exJP 先生は週末に何をなさいますか。 / exKana せんせいはしゅうまつになんをなさいますか / exTokens [何, なん]
items.proposed: exKana: せんせいはしゅうまつになにをなさいますか ; exTokens: ["何","なん"] -> ["何","なに"]. exJP, exEN and exZH unchanged.
items.evidence: 何 before を is なに. The repo's own PLAN-V1.25 says 'なんを is not a possible reading of anything' and corrected n5-g021 for exactly this. Sudachi reads 何:なん here, which is the known Sudachi default that put the error in (the corpus agrees with Sudachi, so this is one blind spot, not two confirmations). Audio: PROOF. The exJP rendered with only 何 replaced by なに (先生は週末になにをなさいますか。) is byte-identical to the exJP audio; the なん substitution is not. The comparative arbiter agrees: なに 0.04103 against the shipped なん 0.06243. dictation-reading-mismatches.json already records '何 なん -> なに, proven (v1.29, instrument 1b)', so the sentence is kept out of dictation but still teaches なんを as the typing target and furigana. The headword なさる is read correctly. The translations are fine.
items.resolution: 何 before を is なに, not なん; the corpus had copied Sudachi's 何:なん default. exKana and the 何 token now read なに. Released back into dictation: 1b confirms the voice says なに (v135-dictation-remeasure.json). Round 2: the review asked whether 何 read なん was a one-off; it was a class of thirteen more (roundTwo below).

items.current: exJP 10歳以下は無料だ。 / exEN Under 10 years old is free. / exZH 10岁以下免费。 / no exKana, no exTokens
items.proposed: exEN: It is free for ages 10 and under. (exZH unchanged; no exKana/exTokens, since this is deliberately display-only)
items.evidence: 以下 includes its boundary: 10歳以下 means aged 10 or younger, and 未満 is the word for 'under 10'. The English 'Under 10' leaves out age 10, which gets wrong the one distinction a 以下 card has to teach, and it is also awkward English. Chinese 以下 conventionally includes the boundary, so exZH can stay. The missing exKana is deliberate: this is one of the 14 pinned display-only sentences (ExampleSentenceTests.sentencesWithoutReadings), because Sudachi reads 10 as いちれい, so there is no reading to check. Optional, outside the example fields: the card gloss 'less than' makes the same boundary error ('... or less / not more than' would be exact).
items.resolution: 以下 includes the boundary (aged 10 or younger); 'Under 10' excluded age 10. exEN now 'It is free for ages 10 and under.'. Display-only by design (digits), so no reading moves. Round 2: meanings.en 'less than' contradicted the corrected example and duplicated 未満's gloss; replaced in place by 'not more than' (removeEN + finalEN in the manifest). meanings.zh 以下 unchanged.

items.current: exJP 三つのうち一つを選ぶ。 / exKana みっつのうちひとつをえらぶ / exEN Choose one from inside the three. / exZH 从三个当中选一个。
items.proposed: exEN: Choose one of the three.
items.evidence: The reading is right. Sudachi gives 三:みっ つ の うち 一:ひと つ, which matches exKana and exTokens. The arbiter puts the shipped reading nearest (0.00951), ahead of the rivals いち (0.06436) and さんつ (0.08357). ~のうち here means 'among / of', not physical 'inside'. 'from inside the three' is not idiomatic English and pushes the card's 'inside' gloss onto a sense the sentence does not use. exZH 当中 is correct. This is a minor translation defect only; the Japanese is natural.
items.resolution: 〜のうち here is 'among / of', not physical 'inside'; 'Choose one from inside the three' was unidiomatic. exEN now 'Choose one of the three.'. Reading confirmed (arbiter: taught 0.00951, nearest). Round 2: the glosses lacked the 'among / of (a group)' sense the example teaches; 'among' and '当中' appended (append-only, finalEN/finalZH in the manifest).

items.current: surface 消しゴム, kana けしゴム / exJP けしゴムを貸してください。 / exKana けしごむをかしてください / exTokens [けし,けし],[ゴム,ごむ]…

items.evidence: This is the same word, but the sentence writes the headword in the kana-field spelling (けしゴム) rather than the card's spelling 消しゴム, which is the standard written form. けしゴム belongs to children's writing before 消 is learned. It passes usesTheWord only because the headword kana field is literally けしゴム. The pattern comes from commit 684493d (the -k loanword batch), where the generator was evidently given the kana field. Siblings n3-k030 「ジェットきに乗る。」 and n2-k117 show it too. This is orthography, not a reading defect: Sudachi けし/ゴム equals exKana. I say 'defect' only because the example never shows the card's own spelling. If the owner considers kana spelling acceptable, downgrade it to ok.
items.resolution: Sentence writes けしゴム for 消しゴム. Refuted by both refuters: same lexeme and same reading, orthography only; exKana correct. Not corrected.

items.current: surface ジェット機 / kana ジェットき / exJP 「ジェットきに乗る。」 / exKana じぇっときにのる / exTokens [ジェット:じぇっと][き:き][に:に][乗る:のる][。:。]
items.proposed: exJP: 「ジェット機に乗る。」. exKana stays じぇっときにのる. exEN ("Ride a jet plane.") and exZH ("乘坐喷气式飞机。") stay. exTokens must be regenerated. Sudachi C gives [["ジェット機","じぇっとき"],["に","に"],["乗る","のる"],["。","。"]].
items.evidence:
The sentence spells 機 in hiragana (ジェットき). No Japanese writer spells the word that way, so the card shows ジェット機 while the sentence never contains that written form. This is also partly a B problem.
How it happened: 684493d (2026-06-04) generated the sentence while the surface was still ジェット, and the LLM copied the kana field ジェットき into exJP. v1.15 H (5bc8596) then extended the surface to ジェット機 and left exJP alone.
Why no gate caught it: usesTheWord in ExampleSentenceTests accepts e.kana as a matching substring, so the literal ジェットき passes.
Side effect: Sudachi splits off き as a standalone noun token (き:き), so the token-lookup chip would land on an unrelated word き.
The reading itself is correct. Sudachi reads the proposed exJP as ジェット機:じぇっとき, matching the taught kana.
Audio arbiter: rendering 「ジェット機に乗る。」 gives byte-identical WAVs to both 「ジェットきに乗る。」 and ジェットきにのる (sha1 1b8ed80de3c9). That is proof Kyoko reads 機 as き here, so the fix leaves the dictation audio unchanged. The script's built-in proof check was silent only because it compares against all-hiragana text, and hiragana じぇっと renders differently from katakana ジェット. Comparative distances: taught 0.06819, はた 0.13119, ひこうき 0.17301.
items.resolution: exJP spelled 機 in hiragana (ジェットきに乗る), a form no writer uses, so the sentence never showed the headword ジェット機 and Sudachi split off a stray き token. exJP now ジェット機に乗る。, exTokens regenerated; exKana unchanged.

items.current: 罰する / ばっする / exJP 「法律を破った人は正しく罰せられます。」 / exKana ほうりつをやぶったひとはただしくばっせられます / exEN "People who break the law are properly punished." / exZH "违法的人会受到惩罚。"
items.proposed: If corrected, the smallest fix is to drop 正しく. exJP: 「法律を破った人は罰せられます。」. exKana: ほうりつをやぶったひとはばっせられます. exEN: "People who break the law are punished." exZH stays "违法的人会受到惩罚。" (it already leaves out 正しく). exTokens: delete ["正しく","ただしく"]; the other tokens are unchanged (Sudachi on the proposed exJP gives the same tokens without that one).
items.evidence:
The reading is correct. Sudachi reads 罰せ as ばっせ (dictionary form 罰する), matching exKana. Arbiter: proof silent; comparative taught 0.02919 vs ばち 0.04295. On the proposed sentence: taught 0.02343 vs ばち 0.04582.
The issue is style only. My own judgment is that 正しく罰せられる is grammatical but an unidiomatic collocation that reads like a translation of "properly punished"; natural choices would be きちんと, 厳しく, 正当に, or no adverb. The earlier review n3-full-review-2026-08-06 (minorItems[22]) flagged the same wording as minor and it was never fixed. The shipped exZH already leaves the adverb out.
It is borderline between "merely unusual" and "unnatural", so I am leaving the decision to a human rather than calling it a defect.
items.resolution: Reading correct (罰せ:ばっせ). 正しく罰せられる is grammatical but reads like a calque of 'properly punished'; borderline style, left to a human. No change.

items.evidence: 金を奪った in this sentence means money: exEN says 'stole my money' and exZH '骗走了我的钱'. It is read かね; きん means gold, so the rider is taught a false reading. Kyoko's audio of the kanji sentence matches かれはわたしをだましてきんをうばった at distance 0.000 (effectively identical), but she also reads 金 as きん where only money makes sense: やたらに金を遣って (n2-b427, corpus かね) is byte-identical to ...きんをやって..., 金がない matches きん at 0.000 (vs かね 0.217), and 彼に金を貸した prefers きん 0.012 over かね 0.073. So Kyoko shares Sudachi's きん default: one blind spot seen twice, not two confirmations. The verdict rests on Japanese knowledge and both translations. The headword span (だます) and the headword kana are correct. The voice also reads 私 as わたし (byte-identical). わたくし with plain だ-style past is a register mismatch, but PLAN-V1.25 declines rewriting 私/わたくし outside the headword, so I propose no change there.

items.current: 驕る/おごる (to be proud, haughty); exJP 奢ることなく努力する。 / exKana おごることなくどりょくする; exTokens [[奢る,おごる],[こと,こと],[なく,なく],[努力,どりょく],[する,する],[。,。]]
items.proposed: exJP: 驕ることなく努力する。 exKana unchanged (おごることなくどりょくする). exEN and exZH unchanged ('Work hard without being proud.' / 不骄傲地努力。). exTokens must be regenerated, which here means only that the first token's surface changes from 奢る to 驕る. In the same change, remove the "n1-g046" line from knownVariantSpelling in Tests/ConjugationDataTests/ExampleSentenceTests.swift (line 88). PLAN-V1.26 notes that list has no staleness check, so the exemption would otherwise stay forever.
items.evidence: The reading is not in question: おごる is correct under either kanji. The problem is the word the sentence writes. From my own knowledge of the standard convention for writing おごる in kanji (明鏡 style): the sense 'to be haughty/proud' is written 驕る or 傲る, and 奢る is written for 'to be extravagant' and 'to treat someone'. Using 奢る for the haughty sense is an older or classical usage (the Heike 奢れる人も), not modern standard spelling. So a learner studying 驕る never sees 驕 in the example, and the kanji they do see belongs mainly to another sense. 奢ることなく努力する can even be read as 'work hard without extravagance'. This is the same kind of case the project deleted in v1.15 G, where 納める's example used 収める, a same-reading kanji with a different sense. It contradicts that commit's reason for keeping this one ('correct Japanese and do teach the word'); that reason was written for a substring gate, not a linguistic review. Sudachi merges the two (its normalized_form for 奢る is 驕る), so it cannot tell them apart and is no evidence either way. On the fix: Sudachi reads 驕ることなく努力する。 as 驕る:おごる, and the arbiter's comparative puts the proposed exKana at 0.03521 against a rival きょうる at 0.09988 (PROOF silent). The rival is not a realistic reading, so this only weakly confirms that the fix keeps the reading. 驕ることなく is a common set phrase. Confidence is medium, not high, because 奢る for this sense is attested historically and some dictionaries list the kanji together.
items.resolution: 驕る taught, sentence writes 奢る. Split vote (1 upheld, 1 refuted): same lexeme おごる, the haughty sense is attested with 奢 (奢る平家), sense and reading match; already on knownVariantSpelling. Not corrected.

items.current: ゆがむ/ゆがむ; exJP 顔が苦痛で歪む。 / exKana かおがくつうでゆがむ; EN 'My face will warp with pain.' ZH 脸因痛苦而扭曲。
items.proposed: exEN: 'My face will warp with pain.' → 'My face twists in pain.' (Nothing else changes: exJP, exKana, exZH and exTokens stay as they are.)
items.evidence: Reading: Sudachi gives 歪む:ゆがむ, which equals exKana, and tokens are consistent. The audio arbiter does disagree. On the real sentence its comparison put ひずむ nearest (0.0257, against 0.0718 for ゆがむ). In my probe sentences, 顔が歪む。 and bare 歪む。 were each at distance 0.00000 from the ひずむ spelling, which I take to mean Kyoko reads 歪む as ひずむ; the script's byte check only compares against the taught spelling, so it never tested that. This is a known voice-side misreading: it is recorded as proven in dictation-reading-mismatches.json, listed in v129-nearest-exclusions.json and dictation-exclusions.json, and g219 is already a named knownVariantSpelling exception. In my knowledge of Japanese, a face contorting with pain is ゆがむ; ひずむ is for physical or signal distortion (板・音がひずむ). So exKana is correct and I found no reading defect. The actual defect is the English translation. The sentence uses 歪む in the 'be distorted' sense of a facial expression, but exEN renders it with the 'to warp' gloss, which in English means material such as wood bending out of shape and is wrong for a face. 'Will' also imposes a future reading on what reads as a general or present statement. exZH 扭曲 is correct. I rated this medium because it is a translation-quality judgement and the reading is not affected.
items.resolution: 'to warp' is for material (wood), wrong for a face, and 'will' imposed a future. exEN now 'My face twists in pain.'. Reading ゆがむ is correct; the voice's ひずむ is already recorded and excluded.
